- When sentiment turns negative (even slightly, e.g., -0.25), reduce forecasted price momentum and shift downward bias, especially in early forecast periods.  
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon after recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), forecast often overshoots by 2–5% in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward adjustment of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, avoid aggressive upward bias; instead, anchor forecast to recent 14-day moving average.  
- Forecast horizon >20 days shows persistent overestimation; apply a 3–5% downward bias for long-term (20+ day) forecasts unless sentiment strongly bullish.
